text: More than three dozen submersible engineers, scientists and explorers signed one letter. They sent it to the company in 2018.
provenance: That same spring, in 2018, an organization of the people who do this for a living — submersible engineers, scientists, explorers, more than three dozen of them — sent OceanGate a letter.

text: The company wanted to take paying passengers down to the Titanic. And no one had ever certified a carbon-fibre hull to carry people that deep.
provenance: He had founded a company called OceanGate, and he wanted to do something no one had done at scale: take paying passengers down to the Titanic.
And no one had ever certified a carbon-fiber hull to carry passengers as deep as this one intended to go.

text: Carbon fibre does not fail the way steel fails. It was hidden damage, accumulating, one cycle closer to a threshold no one had truly calculated.
provenance: It was the hidden damage, accumulating, one cycle closer to a threshold no one had truly calculated.

text: The people who do this for a living wrote to say so. The letter went out in 2018. The dives went on for five more years.
The letter used one word for what could happen. Catastrophic. It was written five years before the dive.
provenance: They wrote that the company's "current experimental approach" could lead to outcomes ranging — and these are their words — "from minor to catastrophic."
Catastrophic. In a letter. Five years before. With more than thirty names behind it.

text: The company declined the check that exists so no one is the sole judge of their own machine.
provenance: OceanGate chose not to do it.
It exists because the people who do this for a living learned, over a century of drowned pioneers, that no single brilliant person should be the only judge of their own machine.

text: The company's answer was a system listening for the hull to break. A smoke detector for an explosion.
provenance: Their safeguard was a system to hear the hull breaking.
They had built, in effect, a smoke detector for an explosion.

text: Physics has never once been talked out of anything. So when the people who knew that tried to say it out loud, how many of them signed?
provenance: And physics has never once been talked out of anything.
